chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fight battles, so that your children may inherit glory.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit for children when their parents engage in jihad?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on the merits of Jihad, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the Prophet’s directive to engage in jihad with the enduring legacy of 'majd' (glory/prestige) for their descendants. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted not merely as military conquest but as the spiritual and social elevation of the family line through righteous struggle, reinforcing the concept of generational barakah. The promise of inherited honor underscores the communal and dynastic significance of jihad in establishing Islamic authority and virtue.
